name: Dysraphic Spinal Cord Lipoma

criteria.description: MRI evidence of lipomatous mass contiguous with spinal cord and associated spinal dysraphism
Presence of neurological deficits consistent with spinal cord tethering or compression
Presence of overlying cutaneous markers such as subcutaneous lipoma, hairy patch, or dermal sinus tract

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI confirmation of spinal cord lipoma with dysraphism plus compatible neurological signs
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological supported by clinical findings; histopathology may confirm lipomatous tissue if surgery performed.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic neurological dysfunction due to abnormal spinal cord fixation
Subcutaneous fatty mass often present at birth
searchTerms: soft fatty mass on spinal area
difficulty walking due to leg weakness

common.notes: Urinary retention or incontinence due to neurogenic bladder
Secondary to spinal cord tethering and dysraphism

searchTerms: abnormal sensations in feet and legs

occasional.notes: Localized discomfort related to spinal abnormalities
Overlying skin abnormality associated with spinal dysraphism
searchTerms: patch of extra hair on skin

occasional.notes: Small epithelial-lined tract connecting skin to spinal canal
searchTerms: skin tract connecting surface to deeper tissues

occasional.notes: Ataxic or spastic gait due to spinal cord involvement

searchTerms: increased muscle tone in lower limbs
loss of bowel and bladder control

rare.notes: Severe spinal deformity affecting lung function
searchTerms: progressive spine curve with lung problems

imaging: MRI showing intradural or intramedullary lipomatous mass contiguous with spinal cord
Evidence of spinal dysraphism such as spina bifida occulta
Tethered cord with low-lying conus medullaris
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic congenital malformation
other: Histopathology confirms mature adipose tissue if biopsy or surgical resection performed

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of lipomatous mass on imaging
May have open neural tube defects
Diffuse epidural fat accumulation without dysraphism
Usually acquired, associated with steroid use or obesity
May enhance with contrast and have different clinical progression

redFlags: New onset bladder or bowel incontinence
Severe spinal deformity causing respiratory compromise
references: Tekkök IH, et al. Spinal cord lipomas and tethered cord syndrome. Neurosurg Focus. 2001.
Pang D. Congenital lipomas of the spinal cord: a review. Neurosurg Focus. 2001.
